title: THE ACHE OF A DIVIDED HOME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And Jacob did so. He finished the week with Leah, and then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife. Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her attendant. Jacob made love to Rachel also, and his love for Rachel was greater than his love for Leah. And he worked for Laban another seven years." - Gen 29:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob works another seven years and finally marries Rachel too. But now the household holds a painful imbalance: "his love for Rachel was greater than his love for Leah." Under one roof live two sisters married to the same man, one deeply loved and one largely unwanted. It is a recipe for years of rivalry, jealousy, and heartache — and that is exactly what follows in the chapters ahead.

The Bible reports all of this plainly, but it does not approve of it. From the very beginning, God's design for marriage was one man and one woman joined together (Gen 2:24), a design Jesus Himself affirmed (Matt 19:4-6). Here we see the bitter fruit of departing from that design — a divided home, wounded hearts, and children caught in the crossfire of favouritism.

We should learn from the pain rather than romanticise the story. Wherever love is divided and people are treated as more or less valued, deep wounds follow. Leah, the unloved wife, would carry an ache that shaped her whole life.

And yet, as we will see, God does not abandon the unloved. The next verse shows us that the one who was overlooked by man was seen and loved by God. Even in the mess of this broken home, God's compassion was quietly at work.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I seen the pain that favouritism causes?
2. Am I treating anyone as more or less valued in my relationships?
3. Do I trust that God cares for those the world overlooks?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard my relationships from partiality and the wounds it brings. Where there is division and hurt, bring Your healing, and help me to value every person as You do. Amen.
